 Nvidia (NVDA) Stock Could Be Undervalued As AI Bets Cloud Cash Flow
 November 5, 2026, 12:32 UTC BA Bailey Pemberton NVIDIA has moved from a very large five year gain to a bumpier few months, and the real question for you now is whether the current US$200.13 share price lines up with the cash the business can realistically produce over time.
 Over the past 5 years the stock has delivered a very large 561.4% total return, which puts a lot of past optimism into the price and makes the link to future cash generation especially important.
 The company is committing billions of dollars to AI partners such as Meta and other ecosystem players, which can reshape both the timing and durability of the cash flows that underpin any Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) based intrinsic value estimate.
 If you'd rather focus on earnings, this one's for you. See what NVIDIA's 25.1x P/E says about the price .
 The issue now is whether NVIDIA's recent price, after a softer 7 day and 30 day stretch, is adequately supported by the cash flows implied in its intrinsic value estimate.
 If you want a cleaner comparison on this AI infrastructure story, line NVIDIA up against other chip and hardware plays using the 53 AI infrastructure stocks .
 Advertisement Is NVIDIA Still Cheap on Cash Flow?
 The Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) model here is built around what NVIDIA can return to shareholders through future free cash flow rather than near term earnings headlines. On the latest twelve month view, the group generated about $126.7b in free cash flow, and the model then assumes that cash generation continues to grow from that base rather than flattening or shrinking.
 Those projections step up to materially higher annual free cash flow by 2031. This is consistent with a business leaning heavily into capital intensive AI infrastructure and equity stakes in partners, instead of running a steady state playbook. Because this DCF output sits substantially above the current $200.13 share price, the model implies the market is applying a hefty discount to those future cash streams. The recent $3b commitment into Meta’s equity raise is a good example of why, because it ties more of NVIDIA’s future cash to AI funding cycles that investors are still learning how to price. Find out what NVIDIA could be worth using our Discounted Cash Flow (DCF) estimate .
 The NVIDIA Narrative: What Would Justify Today's Price?
 NVIDIA's valuation question only really starts to make sense once you spell out the future the current price is pointing to, and that is where Simply Wall St Narratives come in on the Community page. Each narrative links its number to a clear view on how NVIDIA's growth, profitability and risk profile might evolve from here, which gives you something specific to revisit as fresh results, capital spending plans or AI partnership terms emerge.
 Community views on NVIDIA are split between one camp that sees more upside left in the story and another that feels the market is already paying full freight.
 Bull case: 41% undervalued 
 "Nvidia will hit $400b annual revenue in 5 years time, and approximately 90% of revenue will come from data centre customers…" Discover why this Narrative puts NVIDIA at 41% undervalued .
 Bear case: roughly fairly valued 
 "Apply Graham's margin-of-safety discipline to a conservative DCF, using a 9% discount rate, and you get a per-share value somewhere near $200…" Explore why this Narrative puts NVIDIA at roughly fairly valued .
 One more NVIDIA check that belongs next to the cash flow math
 NVIDIA's valuation story is only part of the picture. The people steering the business, and the way their pay is structured, can strongly influence how those cash flows are pursued and protected. See who runs NVIDIA and how they are paid .
